text:
miles: Hey team — first-day setup question. I ran `make dev` and Postgres container starts but migrations fail with: 
```
FATAL:  database files are incompatible with the server
DETAIL: The database cluster was initialized by PostgreSQL version 13, but the server is running version 14.
```
Postgres goes into recovery mode and the container keeps restarting. I'm on an M1 Mac and I pulled the repo from a coworker who used an intel laptop. Any safe way to reset local DB without losing the seeds I added earlier?

irina: Welcome, miles! :wave: That error usually means the PGDATA directory was created by a different PG version or a different architecture image (amd64 vs arm64). If you don't need the old data, easiest is to delete the volume and let compose recreate it. Quick checks: `docker volume inspect` and `docker ps -a` to find the container.

sam: If you want to keep a backup first, run something like this to export the raw data dir to a tar (done from an ephemeral container):
```
docker run --rm -v redwood_postgres_data:/data -v $PWD:/out alpine sh -c "cd /data && tar -cf /out/pgdata-backup.tar ."
```
That gives you a snapshot you can copy off before nuking the volume. We also have `dev/backup_local_db.sh` in the repo for convenience (but the tar trick works everywhere).

irina: Steps I usually follow: 
1) `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml down`
2) `docker volume rm redwood_postgres_data` (or the actual volume name in your env)
3) `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d postgres`
4) run `make dev` — migrations/seed should run and create a fresh cluster.
If you actually used a bind mount (host folder) instead of a named volume, move the host folder out of the way — that folder will also have incompatible files.

devops-bot: Heads up: on Apple Silicon prefer multi-arch or arm64 images. Check internal docs: https://redwood.dev/internal/dev-setup#arm-m1 — using amd64 images under emulation can mask PG version/arch issues.

miles: Thanks! Quick question — when I ran `docker volume ls` I saw a volume called `project_postgres_data` rather than `redwood_postgres_data`. How do I know which one is the right one to delete?

irina: Volume names come from the compose project name + service + volume name. Run `docker compose -p redwood_dev config` to see the resolved names, or `docker compose -p redwood_dev ps` to map containers to volumes. If unsure, look at `docker volume inspect <name>` and check Mountpoint and CreatedAt. The big one with recent size is likely the DB.

sam: Also check `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml config | grep -A2 volumes` to see the declared volumes. If you used a local bind (`./tmp/pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`) you'll need to clear that host directory instead.

miles: Backed up with the tar and removed `project_postgres_data`. `make dev` recreated the DB and migrations completed. All good now, thanks for the help! :tada:
